title: Practice: bind a generator for a rare value
vision: Give a law the valid values it needs when random draws almost never produce one, and see the law exercised with them.
explanation: Laws and generation strategies are authored in LawSpec. Only the implementation changes language.
news: A law over a restricted type needs a valid value to test; a generator or an example supplies it.
contributions: A voucher-loan law refused for lack of a value, repaired once with an example and once with a bound generator. The generator exposes a 14-day bug on real vouchers; every value is checked against the restriction. Evidence covers the two valid vouchers and renewal counts built here.

star.salient: A law over a restricted type needs a value of that type, and a generator supplies one every run.
star.surprise: A law can compile and pass while never meeting the case it names; LawSpec refuses it instead.
star.story: The library gives voucher holders long loans, but vouchers pass two checks that random numbers almost never meet. Without a voucher the law proves nothing; with a bound generator it tests every run and finds the 14-day bug.

hints: Which request would show that a voucher holder gets 14 days? Find the voucher in the failing input.
Compare loanDays 0 with the 28 the law demands. What constant should the formula start from?
Start from 28 and add 7 for each renewal. Load solution shows the complete repair.

stages.title: The law has no voucher to test
story: The library gives a reserve-shelf voucher’s holder a long loan: at least 28 days when a request has at most three renewals. A Voucher is a wrapper over Int32 with a restriction: its number must leave remainder 5 when divided by 30011 and remainder 7 when divided by 30013. Both checks hold for about one Int32 in 900 million.

The law is “for all requests” (a voucher and a renewal count), and nothing in Tests.lawspec or the harness shows a voucher that passes. Predict what Run checks does, then run it. A random draw almost never meets the restriction, so without a voucher the law could only ever check other cases, and it would look as if it passed.

LawSpec does not let that happen. Once the compiler can show a value neither by its boundary search nor from the law’s examples nor from 1000 sampled values, it refuses the law, with the message: “no value of Voucher found by the boundary search or in 1000 sampled values”. It then tells the author to give the law an example whose input holds a voucher, or to bind a generator for the input. The next two steps do each.
stages.action: Run all checks and read the refusal. Explain in your own words what the law would have checked if it had been allowed to pass.
stages.reason: A claim that is never exercised on its restricted input is not evidence. A refusal keeps that visible; a silent pass hides it.
stages.expect: The compiler refuses the law and no checks run. Read the diagnostic: it names the type that has no value.
stages.recovery: Reset this step restores its supplied files and seed. After an edit, use the actual result to judge your version; the story’s prediction describes the supplied files.
stages.syntax: wrapper Voucher is Int32 where … end wrapper declares a restricted type: a number that fails the restriction is not a Voucher. A record field of that type means every Request holds a voucher that passes it.
harnessNotes: This harness only names the law. It supplies no strategy, so the compiler must find a voucher on its own, and it cannot.
A harness changes which inputs are tried, not what the law claims. The next steps change Tests or the Harness so that a voucher exists.
stages.symbol: Voucher 900690137 passes both checks; a random Int32 does not

stages.title: Fix A: show the law one voucher
story: The smallest repair is an example: a concrete input for the law. voucher 900690137 is the smallest number that leaves 5 after dividing by 30011 and 7 after dividing by 30013. The law now has an example whose input holds a voucher, so the compiler has a value to work from.

That is enough to lift the refusal, but it is one voucher. The law is still exercised on a single value of the restricted type, and every later change has the same lone voucher to check. Run the checks and see that the starter, which gives only 14 days, fails the example.
stages.action: Read the example, run all checks and find the voucher in the failing input.
stages.reason: An example is the quickest way to give a law a witness, and it also documents one valid value. It does not vary.
stages.expect: The compiler accepts the law because its example holds a voucher, then the 14-day starter fails the law on that voucher.
stages.recovery: Reset this step restores its supplied files and seed. After an edit, use the actual result to judge your version; the story’s prediction describes the supplied files.
stages.syntax: example "|…| : request = Request record{ voucher = Voucher 900690137 , renewals = 0 } expect … end example binds the quantified input request, then states what must hold. Voucher 900690137 builds a voucher; a number that fails the restriction is rejected.
harnessNotes: The harness is unchanged: still no strategy. The example, not the harness, supplied the voucher.

stages.title: Fix B: bind a generator for the voucher
story: The main repair is a generator: a recipe that builds valid vouchers so that every run draws them. The example is gone from Tests.lawspec; the Harness now declares strategy vouchers, strategy requests and binds the law to requests with use requests for request.

A generator is the right tool when valid values follow a pattern you can build directly. Here, adding 30011 * 30013 to a valid number keeps both remainders, so the strategy draws k from 0 or 1 and builds 900690137 + 900720143 * k. The compiler no longer needs to search: the law is exercised with those vouchers on every run, with renewal counts from 0 to 5.

A found or generated value is always checked against the restriction, so a strategy that built a number such as 900690138 would be caught instead of silently trusted. Run all checks: the law now meets real vouchers, and the 14-day starter fails it, with the failing request shown.
stages.action: Open the Harness tab, read vouchers and requests, then run all checks and read the failing request.
stages.reason: Binding a generator makes valid values part of every run, so the law keeps exercising the case that the restriction makes rare.
stages.expect: The law is accepted and exercised, and the starter fails it on a request whose voucher is one of the two built numbers.
stages.recovery: Reset this step restores its supplied files and seed. After an edit, use the actual result to judge your version; the story’s prediction describes the supplied files.
stages.syntax: strategy name :: T is … end strategy declares a recipe. bind x :: S from g in … draws x from g and uses it below. one of e builds the value e. for law "|…| use requests for request end for law connects the strategy to the law’s quantified input.
harnessNotes: A strategy is a recipe for drawing inputs. vouchers builds a Voucher from one of its two valid numbers: bind k from (one of 0, 1) makes k available in the next expression, and 900690137 + 900720143 * k is the number that passes both checks (900720143 is 30011 times 30013, so adding it keeps both remainders).

requests combines a Voucher from vouchers with a renewal count from 0 through 5 into one Request. The count is wider than the law’s 0 to 3 on purpose: the law’s own guard decides which cases it speaks about, not the strategy.

The binding for “a voucher request gets the long loan” selects the claim in Laws; use requests for request supplies the quantified input request. The generator does not provide the expected answer, and a drawn value is checked against the Voucher restriction before the law sees it.

stages.title: Repair the loan and keep the generator
story: The failing request is real: a voucher holder with no renewals gets 14 days, not at least 28. Change loanDays so a voucher request gets 28 days plus 7 for each renewal, then run all checks again.

As your own challenge, change 900690137 in the vouchers strategy to 900690138 and predict what the run does. That number fails the remainder checks, so the value is checked against the restriction and the run reports it instead of trusting the generator.
stages.action: Repair loanDays and run all checks. Then change the generator to build 900690138 and read what the run reports.
stages.reason: The generator exposes the bug and then keeps guarding the repair: every run draws vouchers.
stages.expect: The supplied starter fails the generated law. After the repair, the same run passes; the challenge edit makes the run report a voucher that fails its restriction.
stages.recovery: Reset this step restores its supplied files and seed. After an edit, use the actual result to judge your version; the story’s prediction describes the supplied files.
stages.syntax: The law needs the result to be at least 28 for 0 through 3 renewals. A formula that starts at 28 and adds 7 per renewal satisfies it.

implementationSyntax.fsharp: In F#, loanDays takes the renewal count as an int and returns an int. 14 + 7 * renewals gives 14 days for none; the repair starts from 28.
implementationSyntax.typescript: In TypeScript, number is the argument and result type. 14 + 7 * renewals gives 14 days for none; the repair starts from 28.
implementationSyntax.javascript: In JavaScript, the function takes the renewal count and returns a number. 14 + 7 * renewals gives 14 days for none; the repair starts from 28.

naming: Use English phrase names for readable claims and descriptive LawSpec helpers. Keep short code names such as add, sort, xs and numbers when they make calls and recipes easier to follow. A phrase starts with "| and ends with |, without a closing quote. A law label identifies the claim; renaming it does not change what the definition checks. The compiler generates target-appropriate names.
